source: research/mcr-colistin-seed.json (the review's Table 1, as transcribed); frame assignments from research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5c–§5e
method: Assign every row whose denominator has been read against its primary to exactly one frame, pool inside the frame, and report the range across frames. Rows not yet read are unplaced and are excluded from both the range and the coverage figures.

frames.why_this_row_is_here: each N is a count of bacterial isolates put through a molecular screen, so n/N is a gene prevalence among screened isolates. Row 19's printed numerator disagrees with its own primary by 100 (49 vs 149, §5b) — the frame is still this one, the cell is the error. Rows 17 (a)–17 (k) are the eleven country slices of one laboratory's stored porcine isolates, PCR-screened for mcr-1 and mcr-2 (§2a, §3, §5f); eight of them were placed on 2026-11-21 22:50Z from the shared methods section rather than from a fresh read. Row 7 (Bangladesh 1,200 / 305) is an isolate screen whose sampling unit is not the isolate: 20 MacConkey colonies picked at random per pooled faecal sample, on 20 broiler farms at three points in one flock cycle (§5j). Its 25.42% is the share of screened colonies, so it belongs to this frame by what N counts and carries a weight caveat the frame's pool does not escape — 1,200 colonies from 60 samples now count twenty times each in its 5.66%. Row 12 (Japan 684 / 90) joins on the same reading: the 684 are swine-pathogenic *E. coli* strains — diagnostic submissions from diseased pigs (diarrhoea or oedema disease) at 23 Livestock Hygiene Service Centres, 1991-2014 — put through a PCR screen for mcr-1 (§5k). It is an isolate screen, but a serogroup-restricted subset: 684 of the 967 strains the collection holds, kept because they fall in four predominant serogroups, so it is 71% of its own source and not a sample of it. Row 15 (Jordan 360 / 143) joins on the same reading — 360 isolates recovered from 385 cloacal samples on 125 broiler farms, then PCR for mcr-1 (§5l) — and its own page prints the phenotype too (209/360 colistin resistant, so mcr-1 is 143/209 = 68.4% of the resistance). Its abstract does not say whether all 360 or only the 209 resistant were genotyped; the printed 39.7% is 143/360, so it is placed here on the paper's own arithmetic and the doubt is written down. Row 3 (China 130 / 75) joins on a full-text read (§5q): the 130 are E. coli recovered from 400 perihepatitis lesioned livers of diseased broilers at Tai'an slaughterhouses, so the frame is the isolate screen but the sampling unit is a diagnostic caseload — and the 75 are the same isolates as the 75 colistin-resistant ones (broth microdilution, EUCAST >2 µg/mL), so mcr-1 here explains 100% of the phenotype and this is not a frame-8 share.

frames.frame: isolates screened for a phenotype, genotyped only in a subset
frames.why_this_row_is_here: Canada genotyped the 12 colistin-resistant isolates of 5,571 and nothing else, so 2/5,571 is a lower bound among isolates tested for phenotype, not a gene prevalence (§5d). India (§5l) is the same design on a different substrate: 253 non-duplicate sewage isolates phenotypically screened, 47 positive, mcr-1 in 5, so 5/253 is likewise a lower bound and 206 isolates were never genotyped. Two caveats the frame now carries: India's 253 are three species (E. coli, Aeromonas veronii, A. dhakensis) and two of its five mcr-1 positives are Aeromonas, so as an E. coli row it overstates; and adding it moves the frame from 0.04% to 0.12%, which moves the floor of the quoted range, because Canada alone had been setting it. Row 27 (Tunisia, §5g) joins on the same design — 836 Gram-negative isolates screened on COL-APSE, mcr genes assayed only in the resistant ones — but on a denominator the primary itself reports and the review does not: 233 E. coli, not the printed 676, which appears in no table of the paper. It is the record's first DENOMINATOR REPLACED BY THE PRIMARY row: the printed cell is retained in its member entry, and the rule is the dict DENOMINATOR_FROM_PRIMARY in this script rather than a special case at the end of a wake. Row 26 (South Africa 50 / 1, §5n) joins on the same arithmetic and not the same selection rule: 50 clinical poultry isolates were phenotyped (none resistant), and only the eight with the maximum colistin MIC from farms with no prior colistin use were PCR-tested, one of which carried mcr-1 — so 1/50 is a lower bound, the tested denominator is 8, and the eight were chosen for expected positivity rather than for a result. That is why this frame's NAME widened in the same pass, from 'genotyped only if positive' to 'genotyped only in a subset': the old name described Canada's selection rule and was false of row 26, whose eight were all susceptible (the paper concedes 'prevalence could be underestimated since not all isolates were tested').

members.denominator_replaced_why: §5g: 676 is a denominator the primary never reports — its abstract prints four E. coli (0.59%), and 4/676 = 0.592% is that percentage pair read backwards. Table 2 of the same paper gives the same four isolates as 1.7% of its 233 E. coli, so the primary's own denominator is taken and the printed cell kept beside it. The design is frame 2: all 836 Gram-negative isolates were screened on COL-APSE and mcr genes were assayed only in the resistant ones, so 4/233 is a lower bound among phenotypically screened E. coli, like Canada's 2/5,571.

frames.why_this_row_is_here: the Portugal row's 227 are enrolled hosts and its 12 are positive hosts; the study's 17 isolates and the isolation medium's own colistin (3.5 µg/mL) are not in either number (§5e). Argentina's 140 are rectal swabs from pigs on six farms — animals sampled, not E. coli isolates (§5i), so 23/140 is host carriage. The frame therefore holds two host species and two sampling designs, and its 9.54% is a pool of those two rows only.
row 18's 128 are retail poultry products; row 5's 1,112 are samples from duck farms and the surrounding water and soil, with 360 isolates recovered from them (§5c, §5e).

frames.frame: one recovered isolate per positive sample
frames.why_this_row_is_here: 147 of 570 Italian meat samples yielded E. coli and one isolate per sample was tested; the primary's own gene figure is 3/147, one more than the row prints (§5e).
the Algerian 103 are colistin-selected mixed-species isolates from 40 environmental samples at 8 sites — not samples, not sites, not E. coli (§5e).
the Chinese 2,649 add raw meat samples, animal samples and inpatient samples into one N and one n, with per-frame positivity of 14.9%, 20.6% and 1.2% (§5d).

frames.frame: colistin-resistant isolates, genotyped for the gene
frames.why_this_row_is_here: Brazil's 490 are not the isolates whose phenotype was tested (that is frame 2's 5,571 for Canada) but the isolates that PASSED the colistin-resistance screen: all 490 were PCR-screened and 8 E. coli carried mcr-1.1, so 8/490 is the share of the hospital's colistin resistance that is mcr-mediated, not a gene prevalence among isolates. The same study gives 8/19 = 42.1% among its resistant E. coli and 8/7,852 = 0.102% among all Gram-negative bacilli (§5h). The Arabian Peninsula row (§5l) is the same quantity from the other side of the table: 75 independent colistin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae from clinical cases in five countries were PCR-tested and 4 E. coli carried mcr-1, so 4/75 = 5.33% is a share of resistance. Its denominator is Enterobacteriaceae and five countries pooled into one N, which is stated rather than smoothed.

unplaced.what_this_is: Every seed row with no frame, in the order the next read should take it. The frames file's row ids are the seed's row ids, so this set is computed as seed minus placed and a placing wake must edit UNPLACED_READ_ORDER in the script; the build refuses otherwise.

members.why: one-page Lancet correspondence (Shen et al. 2016, row ref. 25): no abstract, no PMCID, publisher returns 403. Refused on 2026-11-23 (run 20261123T205650Z) and again on 2026-11-24. Largest open row in the table, and it cannot be closed from this checkout without a copy.

range.bases: the 8 frame rates, not the 32 row rates
range.low_frame: isolates screened for a phenotype, genotyped only in a subset

denominator_replaced.rule: A row whose printed denominator is a quantity its primary never reports may be placed on the primary's own denominator, with the printed cell retained in its member entry, a written reason on the row, and the substitution counted here. Made as one rule (DENOMINATOR_FROM_PRIMARY) so that a class of rows is handled by the record rather than by a wake's judgement at its cap.

what_this_does_not_say: That the frame rates are comparable with each other. They are not: that is the finding.

That the unplaced rows could not move the range. They could — 6 of 38 rows have no frame (the `unplaced` block lists them, in read order, with the reason each is open), and the largest of them (China 1,611 row 2) could widen or narrow it. The range's floor has already moved twice for this reason: it was 0.04% while frame 2 held only Canada, then 0.12% when India joined that frame, 0.18% when Tunisia's primary denominator entered it, and 0.20% now that row 26 is in it.
That any row here is a population prevalence. Every frame is a surveillance design, and the largest block is one laboratory's diagnostic submissions of diseased piglets.
